questions.topic: The Making of Germany and Italy
questions.stem: A school in Italy asks students to trace how a country split into seven states came to be united. In about 75 words, and in steps, trace the efforts that led to Victor Emmanuel II being proclaimed king of united Italy in 1861.

markingPoints.description: In the 1830s Giuseppe Mazzini sought a programme for a unitary Italian Republic and formed Young Italy
Revolutionary uprisings failed in 1831 and 1848
The mantle fell on Sardinia-Piedmont under its ruler King Victor Emmanuel II to unify the Italian states through war
Cavour's alliance with France defeated the Austrian forces in 1859
Garibaldi's volunteers marched into South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1860, and Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of united Italy in 1861

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: In the 1830s Giuseppe Mazzini sought a programme for a unitary Italian Republic and formed Young Italy. Step 2: Revolutionary uprisings failed in 1831 and 1848. Step 3: The mantle fell on Sardinia-Piedmont under King Victor Emmanuel II, to unify the states through war. Step 4: Cavour's alliance with France defeated the Austrian forces in 1859. Step 5: Garibaldi's volunteers marched into South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1860, and Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of united Italy in 1861.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
questions.stem:
After the new government came to power, a district abolished the duties its traders used to pay at every internal border. Officials arrived with a new set of weights and measures, and the council asked everyone to use French as it was spoken and written in Paris instead of the local dialect. Some traders complained that this would cost them money. Others replied that a country with one set of rules and one shared language could not be split into separate little states, each with its own habits. The council answered that the French nation had a duty to free other peoples of Europe from despotism and to help them become nations too.

Read the case and answer the three questions below, each in one line. (i) What two changes did the new government make to trade and to measurement? (ii) Which language did it ask everyone to use, and whose usage of that language was followed? (iii) A trader says these changes will only cost him money. Explain why the council's answer shows that the measures were meant to build one nation rather than to raise revenue.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Internal customs duties and dues were abolished, and a uniform system of weights and measures was adopted. (ii) French, as it was spoken and written in Paris. (iii) Because the French nation declared it its mission to liberate the peoples of Europe from despotism and help them become nations, not to profit from them.

evidence: Internal customs duties and dues were abolished
and a uniform system of weights and measures was adopted.
destiny of the French nation to liberate the peoples of Europe

She tells her friends, and soon students and other members of the educated middle classes in that city have set up a club of their own. They hold meetings and campaigns for a cause they have never campaigned for before. Word spreads to other cities, where similar clubs appear. A local officer notes that the clubs are not armies, yet they have made people ready to listen to the French armies, which are already moving towards Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy.

Read the case and answer the three questions below, each in one line. (i) Who set up the clubs, and what were they called? (ii) Name two of the regions the French armies moved into in the 1790s. (iii) A local officer notes that the clubs are not armies. Explain why the officer's observation still shows that the clubs mattered.
